  • Weierstrass Approximation Theorem
Show solution

  1. First extend the hypothesis to all polynomials.

    If p(x)=∑j=0mcjxjp(x) = \sum_{j=0}^m c_j x^jp(x)=∑j=0m​cj​xj, linearity of the integral gives ∫01p(x)f(x) dx=∑j=0mcj∫01xjf(x) dx=0\int_0^1 p(x) f(x)\,dx = \sum_{j=0}^m c_j \int_0^1 x^j f(x)\,dx = 0∫01​p(x)f(x)dx=∑j=0m​cj​∫01​xjf(x)dx=0. So ∫01pf=0\int_0^1 pf = 0∫01​pf=0 for every polynomial ppp.

  2. By the Weierstrass approximation theorem, there are polynomials (pk)(p_k)(pk​) with pk→fp_k \to fpk​→f uniformly on [0,1][0, 1][0,1]: ∥pk−f∥∞→0\|p_k - f\|_\infty \to 0∥pk​−f∥∞​→0. Put M=max⁡[0,1]∣f∣M = \max_{[0,1]} |f|M=max[0,1]​∣f∣ (a continuous function on a compact interval attains its maximum). Then

    ∣∫01pkf−∫01f2∣=∣∫01(pk−f)f∣≤∥pk−f∥∞⋅M⟶0.\left|\int_0^1 p_k f - \int_0^1 f^2\right| = \left|\int_0^1 (p_k - f) f\right| \le \|p_k - f\|_\infty \cdot M \longrightarrow 0.​∫01​pk​f−∫01​f2​=​∫01​(pk​−f)f​≤∥pk​−f∥∞​⋅M⟶0.

  3. Since each ∫01pkf=0\int_0^1 p_k f = 0∫01​pk​f=0, passing to the limit gives ∫01f(x)2 dx=0\int_0^1 f(x)^2\,dx = 0∫01​f(x)2dx=0.

    As f2f^2f2 is continuous and nonnegative, f2≡0f^2 \equiv 0f2≡0: if f(c)2=η>0f(c)^2 = \eta > 0f(c)2=η>0 at some ccc, continuity would force f2≥η/2f^2 \ge \eta/2f2≥η/2 on an interval, making the integral positive. Hence f≡0f \equiv 0f≡0.
